skill.name: browser-use
skill.description: Automate browser workflows with Playwright MCP. Navigate pages, fill forms, click elements, take screenshots, and extract page data through MCP tools.
skill.summary: Use Playwright MCP to control a browser from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: Most static hits in the generated reference documentation are false positives from Markdown backticks and JSON Schema URLs. Confirmed risks remain in the stdio subprocess path, shell lifecycle helpers, HTTP-capable MCP client requests, predictable /tmp PID files, and browser JavaScript execution guidance. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace subprocess.Popen with shell=False argv execution, or allow only known MCP server commands.
Avoid @latest in npx examples and scripts. Pin a reviewed package version.
Store PID files in a user-owned runtime directory and validate ownership and numeric PID content.
Warn users before authenticated browsing and clear browser state after sensitive workflows.
Prefer named MCP tools and require explicit approval before browser_evaluate or browser_run_code on sensitive pages.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines explicitly document executing supplied browser JavaScript or Playwright code. The risk depends on target page context, but the capability is direct and powerful.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Shared Browser Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires shared browser context across MCP calls. This can retain cookies, logged-in state, and other session data longer than users expect.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions state that shared browser context is required, and the start script enables it. Persistent state is intentional, but it is security-sensitive for authenticated sessions.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Playwright MCP
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows are slow and hard to repeat. This skill provides Playwright MCP commands for navigation, forms, screenshots, and extraction.
actual_capabilities: Start and stop a local Playwright MCP server with helper scripts.
Call MCP tools over HTTP or stdio with JSON parameters.
Navigate pages, manage tabs, click elements, type text, and fill forms.
Capture screenshots, accessibility snapshots, console messages, and network request lists.
Generate Markdown or JSON documentation from MCP tool schemas.
Run browser_evaluate and browser_run_code for advanced Playwright actions.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Playwright MCP, Python, and a runnable browser environment.
Browser actions can affect live sites and authenticated sessions.
Stdio mode can execute shell commands supplied by the caller.
The skill does not enforce rate limits, consent rules, or site terms.

use_cases.title: Test Web Workflows
use_cases.description: Validate login, search, checkout, and regression flows with repeatable browser actions.

use_cases.title: Collect Public Page Data
use_cases.description: Collect public page snapshots, screenshots, and visible structured data for analysis.

use_cases.title: Debug Web Applications
use_cases.description: Inspect UI states, console messages, and network activity during debugging.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Playwright MCP server, open [URL], capture a snapshot, and summarize the visible page state.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], get a snapshot, fill these fields: [fields], submit only after confirmation, and capture a screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Visible Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Visit [URL], collect the visible data matching [criteria], note pagination, and return concise findings with source page names.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser_run_code only for this approved workflow: [steps]. Avoid sensitive fields, record each page reached, and stop the server when complete.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture a full-page screenshot.
output_examples.output: The browser opened the product page, captured a full-page screenshot, and reported the main headings and visible calls to action.

output_examples.input: Submit a demo contact form after I approve the filled fields.
output_examples.output: The form fields were filled, approval was requested before submission, and a confirmation screenshot was captured after submit.

output_examples.input: Extract visible article titles from a news category page.
output_examples.output: Returned a concise list of visible article titles, source section names, and notes about pagination.

best_practices: Run browser_snapshot before clicking or typing so element references are current.
Use approved domains and staging environments for tests that submit forms.
Stop the MCP server and clear browser state after sensitive work.
anti_patterns: Do not browse authenticated accounts or submit credentials without explicit user approval.
Do not pass untrusted text into the stdio command option.
Do not use browser_run_code when a named browser tool can complete the task.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, element interaction, screenshots, and data extraction through Playwright MCP.

faq.question: Does it need a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts start a local Playwright MCP server on the configured port.

faq.question: Can it use authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: Yes, but only with user approval. Shared browser context can retain cookies and logged-in state.

faq.question: Can it scrape websites?
faq.answer: It can collect visible page data, but users must follow site terms, laws, and rate limits.

faq.question: Is browser_run_code required?
faq.answer: No. Use named browser tools for simple tasks and reserve browser_run_code for complex approved workflows.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
